candidate.name: Plandex v2
candidate.one_liner: open source AI coding agent for large projects and tasks
candidate.description: Hey HN! I’m Dane, the creator of Plandex ( https://github.com/plandex-ai/plandex ), an open source AI coding agent focused especially on tackling large tasks in real world software projects. You can watch a 2 minute demo of Plandex in action here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SFSu2vNmlLk And here’s more of a tutorial style demo showing how Plandex can automatically debug a browser application: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g-_76U_nK0Y . I launched Plandex v1 here on HN a little less than a year ago ( https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=39918500 ). Now I’m launching a major update, Plandex v2, which is the result of 8 months of heads down work, and is in effect a whole new project/product. In short, Plandex is now a top-tier coding agent with fully autonomous capabilities. It…

signals.label: 257 points and 81 comments on Hacker News
Posted and answered questions as HN user @danenania

team: Plandex is created by Dane Enania, a technical founder who previously founded EnvKey (YC W18) and works as an engineer at OpenAI on Codex Security.
product: Plandex is an open-source terminal tool that uses multiple AI models to automatically plan, write, test, and debug code changes across large software codebases within an isolated sandbox before applying diffs.
market: The product targets software developers and engineering teams who currently use IDE extensions or CLI tools like Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Code, and Aider to assist with coding workflows.
risks: Direct competition from frontier lab terminal tools and well-funded IDE-based agents like Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, and OpenAI Codex.
Developers may prefer rich IDE-integrated visual interfaces over command-line interfaces for reading and steering live code changes.
Open-source CLI developer tools struggle to capture economic value and build monetizable enterprise business models.
open_questions: How does the founder plan to commercialize an open-source CLI given the competitive landscape of free and low-cost developer agents?
Is Dane Enania working on Plandex full-time given his profile listing as an engineer at OpenAI?
What portion of users convert to the paid cloud service versus self-hosting or using their own API keys?

components.rationale: Plandex is open-source developer tooling and infrastructure rather than software targeting an existing operational budget or displaced contractor cost centre. Its one-liner and launch text frame it entirely as a technical capability: an 'open source AI coding agent for large projects and tasks.'
components.what_would_change: Tie the product directly to displacing outsourced software development agency spend or replacing external contract developer budgets.

components.rationale: The target user and buyer is an individual software engineer or technical developer operating in the terminal. The product is not designed for or sold to non-technical business or operations managers.
components.what_would_change: Reposition and package the tool for non-technical product or business operators building and maintaining workflows without code.

components.rationale: There is extensive independent evidence of real-world usage, including over 15,000 GitHub stars, external contributors, and HN commenters discussing their hands-on experiences comparing Plandex to tools like Aider, Cursor, and Claude Code.
components.what_would_change: Provide verified telemetry or case studies demonstrating paying production enterprise team deployments.

components.rationale: Dane Enania is a YC alumnus (EnvKey, W18) and OpenAI Codex Security engineer with over 800 commits on the repository and deep domain knowledge in AI code generation.
components.what_would_change: Add a dedicated commercial co-founder focused on enterprise sales and go-to-market execution.

components.rationale: The HN launch received deep technical scrutiny regarding multi-model routing, context window limits, CLI usability, and comparisons to Cursor and Claude Code. The founder addressed questions with detailed technical answers regarding diff algorithms and orchestration architectures.
components.what_would_change: Engage broader discussions addressing commercial viability, unit economics, and enterprise pricing models under public pushback.

components.rationale: The project shows strong development momentum with a major v2 release following eight months of development, recent commit activity through October 2025, and over 15,000 GitHub stars.
components.what_would_change: Demonstrate rapid commercial momentum through revenue growth and team hiring.

call_reason: Scores 3/30 on displaced spend — outside the thesis, so the call is Pass regardless of the total.
what_would_change_my_mind: Tie the product directly to displacing outsourced software development agency spend or replacing external contract developer budgets.
